added_models.model: Conjunctival provocation test (CPT) in grass-allergic patients, gp-ASIT+

engagement.confidence_note: Registry record only, no results posted; the quote is the CPT secondary-outcome title. Year is the trial start (2013-08); the record was first posted 2014-06-05.
engagement.note: First member use of the CPT: the subcutaneous gp-ASIT+ dose-escalation study scored CPT threshold shift alongside safety and antibodies.
engagement.quote: Change from baseline in Conjunctival Provocation Test score
engagement.judgement: Model first use is the first subcutaneous gp-ASIT+ study that read CPT (started 2013-08, published as Mosges 2018 doi:10.1111/all.13392); the earlier oral gpASIT+ trials (NCT00833066, NCT01308021) scored field symptoms, not CPT.

engagement.magnitude_basis: CPT reactivity is itself the dosed-patient readout; no separate model number to compare
engagement.confidence_note: Full text read (PMC6175232); CPT reactivity and seasonal CSMS reported side by side in the same Phase III paper. NCT02560948 first posted 2015-09-25, no results posted; EudraCT 2015-002105-11.
engagement.note: In the Phase III (BTT009) the CPT readout fell in dosed patients (P<.001) alongside the seasonal symptom score.
engagement.short: CPT reactivity fell in dosed patients
engagement.quote: LPP-treated group had a reduced reactivity to CPT (P < .001) and, during the pollen season, a lower rhinoconjunctivitis QOL global score (P = .005) compared with placebo group.
engagement.reason: CPT readout moved in dosed patients
engagement.judgement: As for the chamber track, engagement on a human-challenge model is near-tautological: the CPT subjects are the dosed patients. Scored on the model's own readout (provocation threshold, downstream). The open-label dose-escalation (69.8% CPT-nonreactive, Mosges 2018 doi:10.1111/all.13392) is model-side only.

dose.confidence_note: Registry record only, no results posted; the quote is the CPT secondary-outcome title. Year is the trial start (2013-08); the record was first posted 2014-06-05.
dose.note: First member use of the CPT: the subcutaneous gp-ASIT+ dose-escalation study scored CPT threshold shift alongside safety and antibodies.
dose.quote: Change from baseline in Conjunctival Provocation Test score
dose.judgement: Model first use is the first subcutaneous gp-ASIT+ study that read CPT (started 2013-08); the earlier oral gpASIT+ trials scored field symptoms, not CPT.

dose.magnitude_basis: dose: 170 ug cumulative LPP chosen on CPT in the Phase IIb = 170 ug cumulative dosed in the Phase III
dose.confidence_note: Full texts read (PMC5947135, PMC6175232). Phase IIb ran Aug-Nov 2014 (EudraCT 2013-005445-37), prospective to the Phase III (Jan-Sep 2016, NCT02560948).
dose.note: CPT dose-finding picked 170 ug (51.2% threshold shift, P=.023); the Phase III dosed 170 ug and met its peak-season CSMS primary (-15.5%, P=.041).
dose.quote: The mean reduction in CSMS in the LPP vs placebo group was -15.5% (P = .041) during the peak period and -17.9% (P = .029) over the entire pollen season.
dose.judgement: Rule row 'reached, drug worked'. Decision 16: the Phase IIb stated no grade III/IV systemic reactions at any dose up to 370 ug and the Phase III reached the 170 ug course in 89% of patients, so margin_stated true; the three serious early systemic reactions are counted in safety, not here. Paired comparison: the Phase III paper cites the dose-finding but does not restate its CPT result.

dose.magnitude_basis: same 170 ug course in model-chosen dose and confirmatory field trial; the failure is the efficacy failure counted once (peak CSMS 0.15 absolute vs 0.30 pre-specified, p=0.05)
dose.confidence_note: Press coverage reproducing the 2019-12-20 Business Wire release; no peer-reviewed report or posted results of ABT-gpASIT011 found (NCT03724240 first posted 2018-10-30, no results). Sponsor framed the shortfall as masked by rescue medication and filed for judicial reorganization in the same release.
dose.note: The confirmatory Phase III dosed the same 170 ug course and fell short of its 0.30 CSMS primary (0.15, p=0.05); the company restructured and the programme stopped.
dose.short: CPT dose reached, confirmatory trial missed
dose.quote: In the recent Phase III trial (ABT-gpASIT011), gp-ASIT+TM showed a 0.15 (p=0.05) absolute reduction in the Combined Symptom and Medication Score (CSMS) during the peak of the grass pollen (GP) season
dose.reason: CPT-chosen dose failed confirmatory field trial
dose.judgement: Rule row 'reached, failed, abandoned': dose contra derived from efficacy. No higher dose was tried (the Phase IIb's 370 ug arm had not beaten 170 ug on CPT), so this is not a too-low target. Judged on the pre-specified primary (decision 13), not on the sponsor's whole-season framing.

efficacy.confidence_note: Registry record only, no results posted; the quote is the CPT secondary-outcome title. Year is the trial start (2013-08); the record was first posted 2014-06-05.
efficacy.note: First member use of the CPT: the subcutaneous gp-ASIT+ dose-escalation study scored CPT threshold shift alongside safety and antibodies.
efficacy.quote: Change from baseline in Conjunctival Provocation Test score
efficacy.judgement: Model first use is the first subcutaneous gp-ASIT+ study that read CPT (started 2013-08); the earlier oral gpASIT+ trials scored field symptoms, not CPT.

efficacy.magnitude_basis: CPT threshold shift predicts direction only; field peak-season CSMS -15.5% vs placebo against the 20% difference the trial was powered to detect
efficacy.confidence_note: Full texts read (PMC5947135, PMC6175232). The Phase III was powered for a 20% CSMS difference and found 15.5% (P=.041), hence partial. NCT02560948 first posted 2015-09-25, no results posted.
efficacy.note: CPT predicted the 170 ug course would work; the first Phase III met its peak-season CSMS primary (-15.5%, P=.041), below the 20% it was powered for.
efficacy.quote: The mean reduction in CSMS in the LPP vs placebo group was -15.5% (P = .041) during the peak period and -17.9% (P = .029) over the entire pollen season.
efficacy.judgement: Primary endpoint met at P=.041, so same; source_calls_it partial because the effect fell under the pre-specified 20% the trial was sized for. Paired comparison with the Phase IIb CPT dose-finding (model_src); the Phase III cites it without restating the CPT numbers.

patient_trials.quote: Lolium perenne pollen peptides administered over 3 weeks before the grass pollen season significantly reduced seasonal symptoms and was generally safe and well-tolerated.

efficacy.magnitude_basis: peak-season CSMS absolute reduction 0.15 (p=0.05) against the 0.30 pre-specified primary; CPT gave no effect-size prediction
efficacy.confidence_note: Press coverage reproducing the 2019-12-20 Business Wire release; no peer-reviewed report or posted results of ABT-gpASIT011 found (NCT03724240, first posted 2018-10-30). The sponsor attributes the shortfall to rescue-medication use and calls the whole-season effect significant; judged on the pre-specified primary (decision 13).
efficacy.note: The confirmatory Phase III (2019 season, same 170 ug course) missed its 0.30 CSMS primary (0.15, p=0.05); ASIT biotech filed for judicial reorganization.
efficacy.quote: In the recent Phase III trial (ABT-gpASIT011), gp-ASIT+TM showed a 0.15 (p=0.05) absolute reduction in the Combined Symptom and Medication Score (CSMS) during the peak of the grass pollen (GP) season
efficacy.judgement: The CPT model predicted a field effect for the 170 ug course; the same drug's second Phase III fell short of its primary, so the track turns contra (one contra beats a same on the same track, and no source shows the earlier signal reversed). Tier 5 with the Phase IIb CPT paper as model_src; trial_unreported true.

patient_trials.quote: Average daily Combined Symptom and Medication Score collected during the peak of the grass pollen season

safety.confidence_note: Registry record only, no results posted; the quote is the CPT secondary-outcome title. Year is the trial start (2013-08); the record was first posted 2014-06-05.
safety.note: First member use of the CPT: the subcutaneous gp-ASIT+ dose-escalation study scored CPT threshold shift alongside safety and antibodies.
safety.quote: Change from baseline in Conjunctival Provocation Test score
safety.judgement: Model first use is the first subcutaneous gp-ASIT+ study that read CPT (started 2013-08); the earlier oral gpASIT+ trials scored field symptoms, not CPT.

safety.magnitude_basis: systemic-reaction rate: 10.1% of Phase IIb participants (22/198, mostly grade I) vs 10.1% of LPP-treated Phase III patients (37/368), mostly WAO grade 1
safety.confidence_note: Full texts read (PMC5947135, PMC6175232). The Phase IIb's ~150 active patients could have shown a <1% serious-reaction tail and did not (no grade III/IV, no epinephrine); scored partial rather than contra because the harm category and its rate were predicted.
safety.note: CPT dose-finding predicted ~10% mostly grade I systemic reactions and no grade III/IV; the Phase III saw 10.5% mostly mild ESRs plus 3 serious (<1%).
safety.short: SR rate held; serious tail unpredicted
safety.quote: Mostly mild and WAO grade 1 early systemic reaction (ESR) were observed <=30 minutes in 10.5% of LPP-treated patients, whereas 3 patients with a medical history of asthma (<1%) experienced a serious ESR that resolved with rescue medication.
safety.reason: SR rate as predicted, severity tail missed
safety.judgement: Safety split by modality (injected peptide hydrolysate). Model side (Phase IIb full text): 'There were no reports of SRs grade III or IV, anaphylactic reactions requiring the use of epinephrine or fatalities' and 'In 89.9% of the patients, no SR occurred at all.' The predicted harm (early systemic reactions, ~10%, mild) appeared at the same rate; three serious ESRs in asthmatics were not predicted. A checker may prefer contra on the severity miss; the call here follows the predicted category and rate.

added_models.model: BALB/c birch-pollen allergic asthma mouse, sublingual rBet v 1a

efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading. Received 2012-09-04, online 2013-04-16 (PMID 23583462). Soluble rBet v 1a 50 ug/dose was one arm; the paper's focus was an amylopectin-microparticle formulation that did not go into patients.
efficacy.model: BALB/c birch-pollen allergic asthma mouse, sublingual rBet v 1a
efficacy.note: Only animal model found for a member: birch-pollen-sensitized BALB/c mice given sublingual rBet v 1a showed reduced AHR, eosinophilia and Th2 responses.
efficacy.short: Sublingual rBet v 1 mouse model published
efficacy.quote: We demonstrate in a murine model of chronic BP respiratory allergy the efficacy of SLIT with vectorized rBet v 1a.
efficacy.judgement: Opening untested entry at the model's first (and only) published use. The model itself postdates the tablet's positive dose-finding trial, so its first comparison is scored as a retrodiction (next entry).

efficacy.magnitude_basis: mouse AHR, BAL eosinophilia and Th2 reduction vs patient adjusted symptom score -17.0 to -17.7% relative to placebo; no common quantity
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading of both papers; neither cites the other, so the pairing is mine. Retrodiction: the tablet's dose-finding Phase IIb/III was already reported positive by May 2010 (Curr Opin Investig Drugs review, PMID 20419605, used only for dating) and the mouse paper was received 2012-09-04. The 483-patient trial is not on ClinicalTrials.gov (only the 2006-2008 Phase 1 tablet studies NCT00396149 and NCT00889460), so registry_date is null.
efficacy.model: BALB/c birch-pollen allergic asthma mouse, sublingual rBet v 1a
efficacy.note: Mouse SLIT with rBet v 1a cut AHR and Th2 responses; the rBet v 1 tablet had already cut patients' adjusted symptom score 17% vs placebo (P<0.025).
efficacy.short: Mouse reproduced the known tablet effect
efficacy.quote: The average adjusted symptom scores were significantly decreased relative to placebo in patients receiving once daily for 5 months rBet v 1 tablets, with a mean difference of 17.0-17.7% relative to the group treated with placebo
efficacy.reason: Mouse reproduced the known tablet effect
efficacy.judgement: Scored retro, not same (decision 10): the model was run after the clinic knew the answer. Year is the tier-1 patient record (Nony 2015, epub 2015-04-08). Dose, engagement and safety not added for this model: the mouse made no exposure prediction (50 ug/dose twice weekly vs 12.5-50 ug daily tablets), Nony 2015's abstract reports no immunology, and the mouse paper states no safety readout.

patient_trials.quote: Sublingual administration of rBet v 1 tablets is safe and efficacious in patients with BP allergic rhinoconjunctivitis.

considered_not_added: gp-ASIT+ patient ex-vivo basophil / T- and B-cell assays (Shamji 2019, doi:10.1016/j.jaci.2019.02.023): PD readouts measured in the Phase III substudy after dosing, not a model that predicted anything before the trial; no separate prediction to compare.

gp-ASIT+ facilitated allergen binding (IgE-FAB) and IgG4 ex-vivo serum assays (Mosges 2017/2018): drug-induced biomarkers measured in the same dosed patients; no model-side prediction distinct from the CPT track.

gp-ASIT+ animal model: no primary mouse or other animal paper found for gp-ASIT+/LPP (Europe PMC 'gp-ASIT', 'Lolium perenne peptide', 'ASIT biotech' + mouse); the sponsor's 2019 release speaks of 'extensive pre-clinical data sets' but nothing is published.

HDM-SPIRE / ToleroMune HDM ex-vivo patient PBMC or basophil peptide-selection assays: only reviews and a 2013 WAO safety abstract surface; the Circassia biomarker study NCT01949415 posted no results; no primary paper to pair with the field trial.
Grass-SPIRE and ragweed-SPIRE: no animal, ex-vivo or nasal-challenge primary paper found beyond the chamber track already in the draft.

SQ tree SLIT-tablet / birch pollen allergen extract: nasal allergen challenge and mouse searches return only the chamber dose-finding (already tracked) and immune-outcome analyses of treated patients (Wurtzen 2020, doi:10.1111/cea.13788), which predict nothing.
rBet v 1 patient blood DC/PBMC assay: already tracked in the draft (patient-blood-dc-pbmc).
Salsola kali pollen allergen extract (ALK AVANZ Salsola, NCT02065856 tolerability trial): no provocation, animal or ex-vivo model found.
DP/MG/14-1: zero hits on Europe PMC and ClinicalTrials.gov; identity could not be established.
Human genetic model of allergen tolerance: none exists for this class.
In-silico / QSP dose-selection model: none found for any member (Europe PMC QSP / PK-PD / 'in silico' + allergen immunotherapy + dose).
